## PROPERTY INFORMATION
**Service Date:** 2026-05-14  
**System Type:** Type 2 (Aerobic Treatment Unit)  
**System Name:** Main House

## SYSTEM STATUS
The system has a critical pump problem requiring immediate professional attention. The effluent pump is running but drawing no hydraulic load, indicating either a broken impeller, missing impeller, or severed discharge line. This condition creates a risk of motor overheating and failure. All other components are in good condition and the dispersal field is dry with no surface breakout.

## TANK MEASUREMENTS
| Measurement | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Scum Thickness | 3 in |
| Sludge Depth | 8 in |
| Total Fluid Depth | 48 in |
| Solids Content | 22.9% -- within normal range |

The combined solids layer (scum plus sludge) measures 11 inches in a 48-inch fluid column, placing the system comfortably within the normal operating range. No pumping is required at this time.

## COMPONENT ASSESSMENT

| Component | Condition | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Primary Tank (concrete, 1250 gal) | Good | No structural defects observed |
| Effluent Filter | Good | Cleaned and reseated; soiling was light |
| Effluent Pump (0.5 HP, 115V) | CRITICAL | Amp draw 1.6A / nameplate 7.2A = 22.2% FLA. No hydraulic load detected. |
| High Water Alarm | Functional | Tested and operational |
| Electrical Connections | Sound | No corrosion or loose terminals |
| Dispersal Field | Good | Surface dry, no ponding or breakout |

## PUMP PROBLEM -- CRITICAL
The effluent pump is running but drawing only 1.6 amps against a nameplate rating of 7.2 amps. This 22.2% load indicates the pump is operating without hydraulic resistance -- the motor is spinning freely with no fluid being moved. The most likely causes are:

- Broken or missing impeller
- Severed or disconnected discharge line
- Dry-running condition (no fluid in pump intake)

A pump running without fluid cooling will overheat rapidly and fail. The motor is at risk of burnout.

## WORK PERFORMED
- Cleaned and reseated the effluent filter
- Measured scum, sludge and total fluid depth
- Ran the effluent pump through a full cycle and measured amp draw
- Tested the high water alarm
- Walked the dispersal field and checked for surface breakout

## RECOMMENDATIONS

**IMMEDIATE (CRITICAL):**
- Immediate professional attention required for the effluent pump. Do not continue operating the system until the pump is inspected and repaired or replaced. Shut off the pump if possible to prevent motor damage.

**ROUTINE:**
- Continue the current 12-month maintenance interval once the pump is restored to service.

## HOMEOWNER GUIDANCE

### The Pump Problem
Your pump is running but not moving water. This is a serious condition. The motor will overheat and burn out if it continues to run without fluid. Turn off the pump immediately and contact a septic service technician to inspect the pump, discharge line, and intake. Do not wait for the next scheduled maintenance visit.

### Tank Solids
Your tank solids are at a healthy level (about 23 percent of tank volume). Continue to avoid flushing non-biodegradable items -- wipes, paper towels, feminine hygiene products, cooking grease -- as these slow the natural breakdown of solids and can clog the system.
